title: Director of North America Customer Solution Centers and Global Data Center Ops at Dell Technologies Sees Liquid Cooling as a Growth Opportunity but Believes Vertiv Faces Pricing and Delivery Risks
expert: Director of North America Customer Solution Centers and Global Data Center Ops at Dell (current; buys power and cooling for five data centers of 200 racks each); interview 2026-11-10
verdict: A Dell data-center director who buys power and cooling for five 200-rack sites got a Vertiv delivery quote of six months vs nine months at Schneider, though one Vertiv part scheduled for nine months took 12.

Orders / backlog conversion: 🟢 Vertiv quoted six months vs Schneider nine months (first-hand), winning delivery-sensitive AI work; shorter than the 18–24 month power-gear lead times a Google architect cited (SB #64676). → Tenet 5 (share) ↑ {c3}
🔴 A part scheduled for nine months arrived in 12 (first-hand); consistent with mgmt's $100–150M of 2Q shipments slipping into 3Q (SB #64026). → Tenet 5 (execution) ↓ {c3}
🟢 Customers ordering a year in advance to secure production; consistent with mgmt's 12–18 month order-to-delivery (SB #65171). → Tenet 1 (order-led growth) ↑ {c4}
Share in the converged and 800V transiti: 🟢 Racks moving from 20 kW to 100 kW over the next 12–18 months (first-hand plan), requiring liquid cooling. → Tenet 2 (content per MW) ↑ {c5}
Incremental margin vs 30-35% framework: 🟢 A modest premium is acceptable for faster delivery on AI projects (first-hand); first read on delivery-linked pricing. → Tenet 3 (margin) ↑ {c16}
🔴 Facility power delayed one project 18 months regardless of equipment lead times (first-hand). → Tenet 1 (order-led growth) → {c3}

changes: Vertiv delivery quote six months (first-hand) vs power-gear lead times ~18–24 months from a Google architect (SB #64676): shorter here.
Part slipping from nine to 12 months vs mgmt ~$100–150M of 3Q revenue was 2Q shipments pushed out by supply delays (SB #64026): consistent.
Orders placed a year in advance vs mgmt order-to-delivery still ~12–18 months (SB #65171): consistent.
thesis_impact: Tenet 1 (order-led growth): ↑ — customers order a year ahead; site power, not equipment, is the binding delay (18 months on one project).
Tenet 2 (content per MW): ↑ — racks moving from 20 kW to 100 kW over the next 12–18 months need liquid cooling.
Tenet 3 (margin and cash): ↑ — a modest premium accepted for faster delivery.
Tenet 5 (share and execution): → — wins on a six- vs nine-month quote, but one part slipped three months.
